questions.q: How does a 'trace' query differ from a 'list' query?
options: A trace query never uses JOINs
A list query can only return one row
A trace query starts from one specific, known record and walks backward through joins, rather than starting from a condition and returning all matches
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: A trace/audit-trail query begins with a known record (like a specific check number) and follows the joins back to its origin, while a list query filters by a condition to return all matching rows.

questions.q: In the check-trace query, which table does the query start from?
options: AP_CHECKS_ALL
AP_INVOICES_ALL
POZ_SUPPLIERS
GL_JE_HEADERS
questions.explain: The trace starts at AP_CHECKS_ALL (filtered to a specific check_number) and walks forward through AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL to AP_INVOICES_ALL.

questions.q: Why might tracing a single check number produce more than one output row?
options: It never can — a check trace always returns exactly one row
Because AP_CHECKS_ALL always contains duplicate rows
Because the query has a syntax error
Because, as established in Lesson 7, a single check can pay multiple invoices, so the trace returns one row per invoice it paid
questions.explain: Since AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL can link one check to multiple invoices, tracing that check correctly returns one row per invoice it actually paid.

questions.q: In the Receivables trace, what is the correct join order starting from a receipt number?
options: Customer account -> transaction -> receipt
Receipt -> applications -> payment schedules -> transaction -> customer account
Transaction -> receipt -> customer account, with no applications table involved
There is no valid join path from a receipt back to a customer
questions.explain: The trace starts at AR_CASH_RECEIPTS_ALL, through AR_RECEIVABLE_APPLICATIONS_ALL and AR_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL, to RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_ALL, and out to HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS.

questions.q: Why is being able to quickly write a trace query valuable for a consultant during an audit or supplier dispute?
options: It eliminates the need for any accounting knowledge
It automatically resolves the dispute without human review
It demonstrates command of the underlying data model, answering 'what was this payment actually for' faster than clicking through UI screens
It is required by Oracle before any check can be issued
questions.explain: A consultant who can trace a specific transaction quickly via SQL demonstrates genuine understanding of the data model, which is valuable in audit and dispute scenarios.
